residual_identity.statement: |g_t-m_t| = beta*|g_t-m_{t-1}|: the same residual times 0.9, not a new quantity (asserting (1-beta) instead gives a factor-9 error, which is exactly what this check caught)

predictability.statement: Using r_t makes the denominator depend on the current gradient (structurally breaks the "scale is history-measurable" property of 44); at rho=0.999 the effect is only ~0.3% in scale, so it is a structural defect, not a large practical one. Using q_{t-1} removes it entirely.

per_coordinate_collapse.statement: r_t is re-anchored to the group mean q every step, so the coordinate part is only (1-rho)*beta*e_i: the coordinate variation collapses to 4% of a plain per-coordinate EMA

time_constant.statement: The literal residual is 0.9x the standard one, so the time constant is only ~23% slower, not an order of magnitude

boundedness.statement: |u|<=1 holds coordinate-wise even with r=0; the first step is essentially sign(g_1), same order as Adam

index_order.wrong: r_t uses e_t and u_t uses r_t, so the step depends on the current gradient; also q_{t-1}=mean_i r_{t,i} and r_t=rho*q_{t-1}+... are mutually defined
index_order.fixed: update q_t = mean_i r_{t,i} after the parameter step and use q_{t-1} in the denominator
index_order.statement: put the q update after the parameter update and use q_{t-1}

extra_semantic_note.shape: u = m/(|m|+r) is strictly smaller than Adam-style m/sqrt(m^2+r^2) in the mid signal-to-noise band (0.5 vs 0.707 when |m|=r), so it inherits the under-stepping that 43/44/45 already measured
extra_semantic_note.decay: lambda is unspecified; the whole comparison protocol uses lambda=0, so lambda must be 0 or tuned separately
